To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a high education has a positive effect on the probability of having a second child.

(1) a high educational attainment is positively related to second birth rates for one-child mothers; (2) the positive effect of a high educational attainment cannot be attributed to a time-squeeze; (3) a partner with a low educational attainment cannot explain part of the positive effect; (4) a high educational attain- ment of the partner has no effect on second birth rate.
a higher education level has a positive effect on the second birth rate for one-child mothers, that a partner effect cannot explain this, and that the time-squeeze hypothesis is also refuted.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of education on second birth rates among Danish women who had a first child in the period 1980-1985.
the effect of educational attainment on the second birth rate for one-child mothers.
the question of whether the educational system has an effect on fertility in Denmark.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a high educational attainment has a positive effect on the second birth rates for highly educated Danish one-child mothers.
the positive effect on second births of a high educational attainment is due to a positive effect of education on fertility per se.
highly educated women have higher fertility rates than their less-educated counterparts because they want more children.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a highly educated woman is more likely to have a second child than an equally educated woman without a high educational attainment.
the positive effect on second births for women with higher education is not due to either a partner effect or a time-squeeze.
the positive effect is mainly due to the fact that women with a high educational attainment have a higher propensity to have a second child.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the educational attainment has a positive effect on the second birth rates for one-child mothers in Denmark during the 1981-95 period.
highly educated women are not only more likely to become one-child mothers, but they also have a higher probability of having a second child than less educated mothers.
a high education level is an important factor in the decision of whether to have a second child.
